openings.claim: Registration against fixed faces and an insertion stop, followed by clamping, could restore position more consistently than maximizing visible tightness.
openings.delta: Change the joint's locating carrier to plywood corner seats with fixed end-stop tabs for both rods. Adjustable bolt clamps press each rod toward the same two faces; rod width changes clamp travel rather than the locating faces. Cord and elastic keepers must retain every movable part before either rod is released.
openings.prediction: Compared with a tighter fit in the same carrier, deliberate seating before clamping predicts smaller exchange-return errors, including with the 18 mm rod. The nearest rival is that overall tightness determines repeatability and the two awkward trials were incidental. That rival predicts the tighter configuration does at least as well; equal results would not discriminate.
openings.probe: Use at most two configurations of the same adjustable carrier: deliberate datum seating with sufficient clamping, and increased tightness. Per configuration, exchange each original rod five times, then substitute the 18 mm rod for the final two exchanges in the smaller-rod seat: twelve exchanges total. Record target displacement and exchange time after each. Apply four ten-second 10 N lateral trials after exchanges 5, 10, 11 and 12, recording position throughout. A useful result requires both a configuration difference beyond ruler resolution and assessment against the 2 mm, forty-second and loaded-position requirements. Do not deploy from this probe.
assumptions: The unspecified frame geometry permits both seats and stops within 90 mm.
Available bolt lengths, plywood stiffness and keeper reach permit adjustable, captive clamps; these are unverified indispensable capacities.
Fabrication must fit 100 minutes and the complete comparison 20 minutes; schedule feasibility is unproven.

Defeat conditions include insufficient clamp travel, loose stop attachment, plywood crushing, load slip, or any untethered component. If resources cannot provide captivity or adequate load resistance, reject this construction without relaxing constraints.

assessment: A testable candidate, with no claimed fabrication or performance. The supplied return anomaly motivates decoupling location from clamping but does not establish its cause.
